relationships.subject: anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies
relationships.evidence_quote: Anti-CGRP Mbs antibodies induced significant decreases in mean headache and migraine without aura days per month

relationships.subject: cortical spreading depression
relationships.evidence_quote: CSD induces the release of CGRP, which acting on its own receptors, can influence cortical or retinal susceptibility to CSD, through a positive loop.

relationships.subject: blood-brain barrier
relationships.evidence_quote: Because only 0.1%–0.5% of anti‐CGRP‐mAbs cross the intact blood–brain barrier (BBB), the amount of antibody penetrating the barrier during migraine attacks is lower than that required for a significant CGRP inhibition within the brain.

key_findings: Anti-CGRP mAbs reduced headache/migraine days but did not change migraine aura attack frequency in 12 patients.
Authors hypothesize peripheral action on trigemino-vascular sensitization, not on CSD, given limited BBB penetration.
